title: Warm Ham & Swiss Sliders
description: Soft little sandwiches with warm ham, melted Swiss, and a buttery mustard glaze—easy enough for lunch, cozy enough for supper.

ingredients.item: soft dinner rolls or slider buns

substitutions: Use cheddar or provolone instead of Swiss.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Lightly butter or spray a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Without separating the 12 rolls, slice the whole slab horizontally. Put the bottom half in the baking dish.
Layer 8 oz deli ham evenly over the rolls, then add 6 slices Swiss cheese. Put the top half of the rolls back on.
Mix 3 tbsp melted butter, 1 tbsp mustard, 1 tsp brown sugar, 1/2 tsp onion powder, and optional 1 tsp poppy seeds. Brush or spoon it over the tops.
Cover loosely with foil and bake 10 minutes, until the cheese starts melting.
Remove the foil and bake about 5 more minutes, until the tops are lightly golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Cut into 12 sliders and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days. Reheat covered at 325°F or briefly in the microwave.

title: Crispy Bean & Cheese Burritos
description: Crisp skillet burritos filled with creamy beans and melted cheese, made from inexpensive pantry basics.
substitutions: Use mashed black beans instead of refried beans.
Use corn tortillas only if they are large and flexible enough to roll without cracking.
Add leftover cooked rice if you want a larger burrito.

steps.text: Warm the 1 can refried beans with 1/2 tsp chili powder until easy to spread.
Lay out 4 large tortillas. Spread about one-fourth of the beans down the center of each, leaving room at the ends.
Sprinkle about 1/4 cup shredded cheese over the beans in each tortilla. Add optional salsa sparingly so the burritos do not get soggy.
Fold in the sides, then roll each tortilla tightly into a burrito.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Put the burritos seam-side down in the pan.
Cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, turning carefully, until golden and crisp all around and the cheese is melted inside.
Let the burritos rest 2 minutes before cutting. Serve with optional sour cream or extra salsa.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Re-crisp in a skillet or air fryer; the microwave softens the tortilla.

title: Egg Salad Toasts
description: Simple creamy egg salad piled on toast for a fast lunch or light supper.
substitutions: Use plain Greek yogurt for half the mayonnaise.
Serve in a wrap or lettuce cup instead of on toast.
Paprika or dill can replace the green onion.

steps.text: Put 4 peeled hard-boiled eggs in a medium bowl and mash them with a fork until mostly chopped with a few small pieces left.
Stir in 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp mustard, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp black pepper, and any optional pickle or green onion.
Taste and add a little more salt, pepper, mustard, or mayonnaise if needed.
Toast 4 slices bread until as crisp as you like.
Divide the egg salad among the 4 toast slices and serve right away.

storage: Keep egg salad refrigerated in a covered container up to 3 days. Toast bread just before serving.

title: Creamy Cucumber Dill Salad
description: Cool sliced cucumbers in a simple creamy dill dressing—fresh, inexpensive, and especially good beside warm comfort food.

ingredients.item: white vinegar or apple cider vinegar

substitutions: Use plain Greek yogurt instead of sour cream.
Use 1 tbsp fresh chopped dill instead of dried dill.
A pinch of garlic powder can be added if you like.

steps.text: Thinly slice 2 medium cucumbers and optional 1/4 small red onion. Put them in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, stir together 1/4 cup sour cream, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp dried dill, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the cucumbers and toss until evenly coated.
Serve immediately for the crispest texture, or chill 10 to 20 minutes first if you prefer it colder.

storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days. The cucumbers release water as they sit, so stir before serving.
